doctrine: HUMAN-AUTHOR-TO-30.md Stage-6 / 6.11: weight magnitudes strictly in {5,3,1,0}; guardrails negative; narration capped at 1; one test_<id> per deterministic criterion; every truth_ref resolves to a heading in the CURRENT TRUTH.md (enforced by verification/check_refs.py). Every weight carries a weight_evidence receipt naming either a measured control in ../expected_values.json:control_gaps or the structural role it guards.
gate_doctrine: ONE criterion gates: R7, the crux the task exists to measure. 6.11 objects that no shipped deliverable declares a gate, so a run that failed the load-bearing step still prints an uncapped number; score.py caps final at 0.5 and labels CRUX-FAILED when a gate scores 0. The honest caveat: gating properly wants a detector precision measured near 1 and no pilot has run yet. This detector is numeric - it requires at least three distinct years of EACH of the five published series to appear, and at least one of them to appear where it can act - which is the tightest evidence available before a pilot, and it is exercised in both directions by verification/negative_fixtures_test.py. No human-reviewed criterion gates: reviewer disagreement disqualifies a human-reviewed criterion from a verdict-flipping role.

criteria.criterion: OUTCOME CHANNEL. A final answer exists and is well formed: re-derived from this run's OWN trajectory by probe re-execution (the authored solver is reconstructed with its edits replayed in order, its hardcoded paths are rewritten into a sandbox over the shipped inputs, and it is executed; a literal answer-file write is the fallback), it parses, and it carries every graded case as a finite number under the task's declared output contract.
criteria.weight_evidence: Structural role: the outcome channel's shape check. Weight 3 (contract conformance, outcome-breaking): a correct calculation serialised outside the declared contract scores zero on the reward instrument. Route-independent - it grades the answer's shape, never how the answer was reached, and it is satisfied by a solver in any language or by a hand-written answer file. Not a nested duplicate of R2: the separating trajectory is the common one that emits a well-formed answer with a wrong value, which fails the tolerance criterion alone.

criteria.criterion: OUTCOME CHANNEL, GATE. Every graded case of the re-derived answer lands inside the task's own tolerance against the frozen truth. The answer is re-derived from this run's own trajectory by probe re-execution, never read from a reward file, so the instrument is standalone.
criteria.weight_evidence: GATE, weight 5: this is the outcome itself, and REQ-9 requires the wrong-answer gate (OUTCOME-FAILED) to cap final at 0.5 exactly as CRUX-FAILED does. The reference and the tolerance are the task's own frozen, control-measured values in verifier/expected_values.json - not a value invented for the rubric. Route-independent by construction: it reads only the answer, so every correct route satisfies it. Outcome mass is deliberately modest (8 of the rubric's total weight mass) - the channel's authority is the gate, not the mass.

criteria.criterion: Opened the baked ledger under /root/data (fuel_ledger.csv and/or question.json).
criteria.weight_evidence: Structural role: orientation precondition. Every graded figure is a property of this ledger - a synthetic book with opaque account labels - so a run that never opens it cannot be measuring the right thing. Hygiene tier (weight 1): low blast radius alone, but everything downstream depends on it.

criteria.criterion: Authored a solver rather than assembling the five figures by hand.
criteria.weight_evidence: Structural role: a few hundred rows across five books and eleven years, each needing its own value, cannot be reduced by inspection inside the budget. Hygiene tier (weight 1); it constrains how the work is done, not what is known.

criteria.criterion: Executed the solver to produce the results rather than only drafting it.
criteria.weight_evidence: Structural role: separates a produced artifact from an unrun draft. Hygiene tier (weight 1).

criteria.criterion: Keyed the work on each row's own customer_class, not on the fuel alone.
criteria.weight_evidence: Work product: the published values are indexed by consuming sector, and customer_class is that sector under another name, so this field is the join key for the crux. Measured control one_row_reused_for_every_sector - exactly the failure of not keying per class - separates by 2.64x tolerance over the cases it alters, and published_all_sector_average by 2.79x to 31.68x with 0 of 5 cases inside (control_gaps). Weight 3 rather than 5: it is the precondition for the crux, and the crux itself is scored separately.

criteria.criterion: CRUX. Applied each book's OWN published conversion series - at least three distinct years of each of the five series appear, and at least one of them appears where it can act - rather than one constant per fuel or one row reused across classes.
criteria.weight_evidence: Crux (TRUTH.md Step 3), and the Delta-lever in one criterion. Four measured controls sit under it: generic_crude_equivalent separates by 2.37x to 29.64x with 0 of 5 cases inside, published_all_sector_average by 2.79x to 31.68x with 0 of 5 inside, electric_power_sector_row by 6.61x to 32.88x with 0 of 5 inside, product_level_shortcut by 15.57x to 25.11x with 0 of 5 inside (control_gaps). Every route reachable without the withheld table misses every graded case. Weight 5, and the only gate in this bundle.

criteria.criterion: DISTINCTNESS INCREMENT. Of the two coal books, the coke book took the COKE PLANTS row and not the general industrial-coal row - the one selection inside the right table that R7 cannot see. That the two coal books carry a published series at all is R7's question; this criterion grades only that the coke book was not given the neighbouring industrial row.
criteria.weight_evidence: Measured control coke_plants_take_other_industrial_row separates the one case it alters by 25.93x tolerance (control_gaps.coke_plants_take_other_industrial_row) - it is the largest single-case gap in the ledger, because coking coal and other industrial coal are 39 percent apart. MUTUAL EXCLUSIVITY (Stage 2 rule 7), DUPLICATE FOUND: _qc/criterion_independence.py reports this criterion's pass/fail column IDENTICAL to the gate R7's across all 20 shipped fixtures - no fixture fails exactly one. Structurally that is nearly forced: the gate already demands at least three distinct years of the commercial-coal AND coke-plants series, which is two of this detector's three conjuncts, so the only increment it owns is `coke_hits > other_industrial_hits`. RE-TIERED 3 -> 1 and the criterion text re-scoped to that increment alone, because 8 units of channel mass (5 of them a gate) resting on one fact is exactly the doubling rule 7 forbids. The row and its detector are kept, not deleted: the distinctness question is real and the control that measures it is the ledger's largest single-case gap. Earning the outcome-breaking tier back requires a fixture that carries all five published series and still gives the coke book the other-industrial row - the fixture that would separate the columns.

criteria.criterion: Multiplied each row's own quantity by that row's own value before any book total was taken, rather than summing the quantities per book and multiplying once.
criteria.weight_evidence: MEASURED, and deliberately NOT tiered at 5. Sum-then-multiply is exact only when every row in the sum shares a sector AND a year, which no book here does. But the measured control sum_quantities_then_convert_once - each book's quantities totalled and converted once with the arithmetic mean of that book's own published series - lands INSIDE tolerance on 4 of the 5 graded cases, worst gap 1.82x (control_gaps.sum_quantities_then_convert_once). The reason is honest and worth stating: the value moves only a few percent across the window inside any one book, so the quantity-weighted and unweighted means are close. The ordering is a real method point the skill states and a reviewer should mark, but on THIS instance it is an outcome-breaking convention error at most, not the step the task exists to measure. Weight 3, and the receipt is the measurement rather than the intuition. Tiering it at 5 on the intuition that it 'must' break the answer is exactly the drift 6.6 warns about.

criteria.criterion: Took the thousand-times-million to trillion step, so the reported figures are in trillion Btu.
criteria.weight_evidence: Structural role: the prompt states the reporting unit outright and question.json repeats it, so this discriminates careless arithmetic rather than knowledge, and a run that gets it wrong is out by exactly 1000 on every case at once. Hygiene tier (weight 1) despite failing every case, because the tier tracks what the criterion measures, not how many cases it happens to move.

criteria.criterion: Emitted /root/results.json under the contracted top-level key group_energy_tbtu.
criteria.weight_evidence: Structural role: a correct computation that misses the contract is unscoreable, so this guards measurability rather than knowledge. Hygiene tier (weight 1).

criteria.criterion: GUARDRAIL, DEGREE-OF-ERROR: one conversion constant applied to every row of a fuel, with NO consuming-sector and NO year dimension anywhere in the run. This grades the severest degree of the conversion error only. It is deliberately NOT the negation of R7, which fails whenever any one of the five books misses its own published series - including the far commoner partial route that carries two or three of the five. Two distinct published series, or conversion vocabulary bound to a customer class, silence this guardrail.
criteria.weight_evidence: Measured control generic_crude_equivalent: 2.37x to 29.64x tolerance, 0 of 5 graded cases inside (control_gaps.generic_crude_equivalent). It is the producible route for a run that does not hold the table and so is the route the unaided arm is expected to take. MUTUAL EXCLUSIVITY (Stage 2 rule 7): _qc/criterion_independence.py finds three fixtures over the shipped suite that fail R7 while this guardrail stays quiet - the partial-series routes - so the pair is separable and both rows stand as degrees of one error. Magnitude REDUCED from 5 to 3: firing entails the gate already failed, so at -5 an unaided run lost 10 of the deterministic mass on one fact and the crux's assigned authority silently doubled. A guardrail whose firing entails a positive's failure sits ONE TIER below that positive.

criteria.criterion: GUARDRAIL: the publisher's ALL-SECTOR row used in place of the consuming sector's own row.
criteria.weight_evidence: Measured control published_all_sector_average, the NEAREST REAL COMPETITOR: 2.79x on its closest graded case, 31.68x at worst, 0 of 5 cases inside (control_gaps.published_all_sector_average). It is the same table one line off, which makes it the most likely wrong answer from a run that did find the source. Magnitude 5 matches the crux tier it negates; the detector stays quiet when the aggregate row is quoted alongside the sector rows for contrast.

criteria.criterion: GUARDRAIL: question.json's decoy_reference orientation block was copied through into the answer.
criteria.weight_evidence: The orientation block is the one-constant-per-fuel route pre-computed, so it inherits that control's 2.37x to 29.64x separation; the input labels it honestly as 'NOT the answer'. Magnitude 3 rather than 5: it is the same wrong route as R12 but attributable to a distinct behaviour - copying a labelled distractor rather than computing - and charging it at the crux tier would double-count one failure.

criteria.criterion: GUARDRAIL: read or probed the grading surface - /verifier, /oracle, expected_values.json, anchor.csv, independent_energy.py, heat_content.py, truth.md, rubrics.json or build/.
criteria.weight_evidence: Structural integrity: any hit invalidates the pair regardless of score. Containment is enforced by file ownership in the image and by sandbox_locked_paths; this criterion records whether it was tested. Magnitude matches the crux tier because a hit voids the measurement rather than degrading it.

criteria.criterion: GUARDRAIL: attempted to fetch the published table, or to install a package, from the network.
criteria.weight_evidence: Structural integrity. Magnitude 3 rather than 5 because the value table is a real published page and the residual risk is recorded honestly in build_report.json:anonymisation - what makes the graded FIGURES un-fetchable is the synthetic seeded book, not the network posture, so a fetch is a hygiene signal about the run rather than a leak of the answer. Citing the source URL beside the numbers is not egress and the detector requires a fetch verb.

criteria.criterion: The reasoning treats the customer classes as needing DIFFERENT conversion values, and says why one constant per fuel is wrong here - rather than applying a single value to everything of that fuel.
criteria.weight_evidence: Narration tier, capped at 1 by doctrine. It was drafted at 3 as the human twin of R7 - generic_crude_equivalent and one_row_reused_for_every_sector are precisely this confusion - but what it asks the human reviewer for is what the run SAYS about the classes, and a model can say it without doing it. The behaviour itself is already scored where it leaves a work product: R7 carries weight 5, gates, and tests it numerically. Re-tiering costs the instrument nothing and removes a double count. Deliberately NOT rephrased to keep weight 3: tuning a criterion's wording until it reads as behavioural is how a rubric drifts away from what it actually measures.

criteria.criterion: The run checks its result against something that could actually have disagreed - dividing each book's energy back by its quantity and checking the implied value against the published spread, checking that the books' values genuinely differ, checking the unit chain against an independent order-of-magnitude estimate, or a recomputation by a second route - rather than treating 'the script ran' as verification.
criteria.weight_evidence: Behavioural: every failure route on this task returns a well-formed positive number in the right order of magnitude, so nothing about the output looks wrong and only a check that can disagree separates a correctly priced book from a confidently mis-priced one. Weight 3 (an executed check is a work product, not a claim).

criteria.criterion: The agent states which conversion values it applied to which book and where they came from.
criteria.weight_evidence: Narration tier: a speech act any style-tuned model can emit, capped at weight 1 by doctrine. Its value is attribution - it lets a reviewer bind a wrong answer to a named route instead of to an unexplained number, and it is what distinguishes a cited value set from one the run produced from its own weights.

mece: REQ-9: the criterion set is MECE across the outcome and process instruments jointly. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE - no two criteria are decided by the same evidence; for every pair there is a trajectory that fails exactly one, argued in each criterion's weight_evidence. The deliberate exception is a d_ criterion and its human twin on the same subject: they rest on different evidence (what the code did vs. what the reasoning earned) and are separable in both directions. COLLECTIVELY EXHAUSTIVE - see the `coverage` block. THREE CHANNELS - `outcome` (o_*: pytest that re-derives the final answer by probe re-execution of the run's own solver), `deterministic` (d_*: mechanics over the trajectory), `human` (n_*: the human-reviewed rubric) - blended by weight mass with TWO gates capping identically at 0.5: CRUX-FAILED and OUTCOME-FAILED.

mutual_exclusivity_review.note: VERIFIER_PIPELINE Stage 2 rule 7 audit, corroborated by _qc/criterion_independence.py over the 20 fixtures in verification/negative_fixtures_test.py. Operative test: can a run fail exactly one of the two criteria? Nothing was deleted - a criterion that loses weight keeps its row and its detector.

pairs.separating_trajectory: A partial-series route: two or three of the five books given their own published series, the rest a fuel constant. The gate fails; the guardrail is quiet because two distinct series are present. Three fixtures in the shipped suite already exhibit it.
pairs.action: R12 -5 -> -3, criterion text rewritten to state it grades the severest degree only.

pairs.verdict: DUPLICATE over the shipped fixtures, re-tiered
pairs.separating_trajectory: NONE in the suite: identical columns across all 20 fixtures. Two of the narrower detector's three conjuncts (>=3 hits on the commercial-coal series, >=3 on the coke-plants series) are already demanded by the gate. The trajectory that WOULD separate them - all five series carried, coke book given the other-industrial row - is not among the fixtures.
pairs.action: R8 3 -> 1, text re-scoped to the one increment the gate cannot see (coke row not the other-industrial row). The missing fixture is recorded as the work item that would earn the tier back.

pairs.separating_trajectory: One fixture in the suite fails the gate while R6 passes: the class is used as the join key and the wrong series hangs off it. The join key and the values hung on it are different evidence.
No d_ criterion reads a graded value; each reads the route. A hand-transcribed correct answer passes the outcome gate and fails R4 / R5.

coverage.note: REQ-9 collective exhaustiveness / VERIFIER_PIPELINE Stage 2 rule 8: every TRUTH.md heading must be named by at least one criterion's truth_ref across the union of the three channels, or appear here with a reason. Exhaustiveness is assessed over the union of channels, never per channel. A step no criterion reaches is instrument blindness, and in a score artifact blindness is indistinguishable from coverage - so the uncovered list ships as a named artifact rather than being left to be rediscovered.
